reader.requirement: At 1985, when an OCCURS ... DEPENDING ON data-name-1 is written in a record description entry that contains the EXTERNAL clause, data-name-1 must be an item with the external attribute (in an EXTERNAL working-storage record, the same or another, or in a record of an EXTERNAL file, §1985:II.6.2.2.2.3) described in the same program's Data Division; an internal object (working-storage, linkage, a non-external file's record) or an external item described in a containing program is refused, and a fixed OCCURS needs no object. The witness covers part of the refusal half.
reader.edition-search: Re-read at pin 524fb73a18 after wave 20262135 group A (kb/Work PB2628's branch) moved the external-attribute test from DataBinder.IsInExternalRecord(item, files) to the one fact DataItem.HasExternalAttribute (the root's EXTERNAL clause, its EXTERNAL type, or root.RecordOfFile is { IsExternal: true }, RecordOfFile written by FileModel.AddRecord for every FD and SD record). grep for Year, DialectLevel, CobolVersion, Edition in OdoResolvePass.cs#DependingAttributeFault, DataItem.cs#HasExternalAttribute and DataBinder.Odo.cs#IsDescribedInContainer: no edition switch; binder.Edition is the diagnostic sink and ed.Cite picks the citation only.

reader.notes: Re-read of the moved code (the same seven probes re-run at --std 85 on this tree print what the first read recorded). OdoResolvePass.Run asks DependingAttributeFault for every ODO object: the table record's own EXTERNAL clause or EXTERNAL type is the trigger (table.Root.HasExternalClause || ExternalFromType), DataItem.HasExternalAttribute the object's attribute (EXTERNAL working-storage records and every record of an EXTERNAL file, §1985:II.6.2.2.2.3), and IsDescribedInContainer the 'same Data Division' half. A table in an EXTERNAL file's record with an internal object is accepted, reading SR8's 'record description entry containing the EXTERNAL clause' literally; that is the one interpretive point, unchanged by the move. Diagnostics cite §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR8 at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: Adversarial pass against the moved fact (the FD half now read off DataItem.RecordOfFile rather than a scan of the files). Probes at --std 85 on this tree (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/finish-worktree-wf_46d3a156-23e-9/refute/): x1_fd2nd.cob, the counter a level-05 item of the SECOND record of an EXTERNAL FD, is accepted and the extent follows it ('B [AB]', exit 0), so every record of the file carries the attribute (§1985:II.6.2.2.2.3: 'the data records and the data items attain the external attribute'); x2_sd.cob, an SD record's counter, is refused COBOL2788 'does not possess the external attribute' (a sort-merge file's records are always internal, II.6.2.2.2.3); x5_extnotext.cob, the counter in a record of a non-external FD H while another FD F IS EXTERNAL, is refused COBOL2788 (the attribute is the record's own file's, not any file's). The first refutation's r6-fwd.cob ('[ABC]', exit 0) and r6-77.cob (COBOL2788) print as before. cite.py: 'OK §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR8 (5.8.3 Syntax Rules) the text is in SR8'. The literal reading of 'record description entry containing the EXTERNAL clause' (c6-c1-extfd accepted) stands for the reason the first refuter gave.
